SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is a high-quality franchise with dominant US market share (~15%), strong brand recognition, and a vertically integrated store network of 5,000+ locations that provides pricing power and customer stickiness. Q1 2026 results showed solid YoY growth: revenue +6.8%, EPS +7.5%, with all segments contributing. The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 EPS guidance of $10.70-$11.10 (or $11.50-$11.90 adjusted per some sources), and management continues disciplined capital allocation with $773M returned to shareholders in Q1. ROE remains strong at ~59-65%, and gross margins are healthy at ~49%. However, several factors temper enthusiasm: (1) QoQ trajectory is weak with revenue -10.9% and EPS -35.8% from Q3, though this is partly seasonal; (2) operating cash flow was only $139M in Q1 vs $1.31B in Q3, reflecting seasonal working capital build; (3) total debt of $9.3B with debt-to-equity of 2.1x is elevated; (4) raw material inflation guidance was raised to low-to-mid single digits; (5) DIY demand in Consumer Brands remains soft. On valuation, the stock trades at P/E 29.5x, near the low end of its 365-day range (28.5-37.1), and P/B of 17.3x is also at the low end (16.7-22.1), suggesting the stock is relatively cheap vs its own recent history. The stock hit a 52-week low of $301.46 on May 15, 2026, and is down ~14% over the past quarter. This pullback, combined with an earnings beat (EPS $2.35 vs $2.27 consensus) and institutional buying, creates a modest near-term rerating opportunity. However, the macro backdrop is challenging with rising 10-year yields (4.57%), elevated oil prices ($100/bbl), and housing market headwinds that limit the upside case. The score reflects a solid franchise at a reasonable valuation with modest near-term catalysts, but tempered by cyclical headwinds and elevated leverage.
